Users switching from Windows to Mac rarely encounter software limitations. All major PC applications run on Mac, and there are also many utilities exclusive to Mac.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games have never performed better on Mac, whether through official or unofficial channels……

Apple has an exclusive Game Porting Toolkit designed to help developers evaluate how their Windows games perform on Mac. Its design philosophy is to encourage and facilitate developers in porting games to the Mac platform.

However, Macworld's Filipe Esposito points out that this toolkit has also been used by some players to run Windows software unofficially on Mac, and he himself is one of them. He stated that the latest test version brought a leap in performance, citing GTA V as an example.

I spent several days testing the Beta version of Game Porting Toolkit 4 on a MacBook Pro with M4 Pro, and found that the performance improvements fundamentally changed the experience of running demanding Windows games…… Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB memory, under identical game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to approximately 176 fps on GPTK 4 Beta—an increase of about 66%. The game ran very smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledged that not every game sees such significant improvements, but he hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
